images.caption: Figure 8 The MemoProBench data construction pipeline. We scan a target object over the full Ego4D clip, merge visible segments separated by at most 8 s into a single appearance, and use its first and last visible timestamps to define the trigger window (Step 1). An LLM proposes episodic and semantic memory evidence, which is iteratively checked by a worth-triggering gate to form a grounded memory bubble (Step 2). We then condition a categorized event timeline on a personalized persona and render its events into a stream of visual-action and conversation captions (Step 3), before model QC and human review (Step 4).

Figure 5 Overview of MemoProAgent. The agent proactively observes the current environment and uses the observed entities to retrieve episodic and semantic memories. A gate selects and refines evidence worth surfacing, and the generator combines it with the observation to decide whether and what to say. Unlike Standard RAG, which fills <evidence> with top-k raw passages at every step (Figure 4), MemoProAgent fills it with refined evidence only when it is worth intervening on, and with none otherwise.
images.nearby_text: Generator loop. At each decision point, the generator follows a two-round agentic loop: observe -> retrieve -> gate -> decide (Figure 5). Memory construction. We organize the user's long-term memory as a graph with two layers: an episodic layer and a semantic layer.
